name: Pandoc
build_recipe: The binaries are the official GitHub release assets of jgm/pandoc tag 3.12 (https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/releases/tag/3.12); their sha256 and size were re-verified here by downloading all five assets (engines.json .upstream/Filee/src/Filee.Engines/Infrastructure/engines.json is the source of the URLs). They are produced from the pandoc repository at tag 3.12 (commit 381230ee36d8fa871c28f8982e22579f1a8f723b; verified via git ls-remote and a shallow clone) with GHC 9.10.x and cabal 3.14 by the workflow .github/workflows/release-candidate.yml at that tag (https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/3.12/.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml): the windows job runs `cabal build -fembed_data_files -fserver -flua pandoc-cli`, the macos job runs macos/make_macos_release.sh (`cabal update; cabal build all -fembed_data_files -fserver -flua -fhttp`, GHC 9.10.3), and the linux tarballs/debs come from linux/make_artifacts.sh (same feature flags). The repo pins no dependency plan: there is no cabal.project.freeze and no stack.yaml/stackage snapshot at tag 3.12, and cabal.project carries only a handful of lower-bound constraints, so the Hackage closure is resolved against the live index at build time. The exact resolution used for this release is recovered from the build log of GitHub Actions run 36516933402 (https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/actions/runs/36516933402, 2026-09-29T03:23Z, head commit 1539a541f5f7239c6f0a221985f24d1d7be6062a which differs from tag 3.12 only in changelog.md), fetched with `gh run view --log`: each job printed the cabal plan header "In order, the following will be built" with `Build profile: -w ghc-9.10.3` and every entry marked "(requires download & build)" (cold cache). That plan lists 235 packages in the macos job and 236 in the windows job (the difference is zlib-clib, needed on Windows only); the union is 236 rows, of which 4 are the in-repo packages pandoc, pandoc-cli, pandoc-lua-engine and pandoc-server (covered by the pandoc git source above). The remaining 225 rows are pinned here as their Hackage tarballs (https://hackage.haskell.org/package/<name>-<version>/<name>-<version>.tar.gz); for each one the tarball was actually downloaded here, its sha256 and size computed, and its license read from the `license:` field of the .cabal file inside the tarball. GHC boot libraries (base, bytestring, containers, text, template-haskell, ...) ship with GHC and are intentionally not listed. The linux and macOS-arm64 jobs are not part of that workflow run, so their resolutions were not captured separately; they resolve against the same index and are assumed to match this set (only the OS-conditional zlib-clib differs in the captured plans). The shipped binaries statically link these libraries, so this list is the Corresponding Source closure for the GPL-2.0-or-later pandoc binary.

sources.name: pandoc
sources.note: jgm/pandoc at tag 3.12 (lightweight tag -> commit 381230ee36d8fa871c28f8982e22579f1a8f723b, verified with git ls-remote and a shallow clone). Contains all four shipped Haskell packages (pandoc, pandoc-cli, pandoc-lua-engine, pandoc-server) plus the data/ tree embedded into the binary by -fembed_data_files. No .gitmodules at this commit. pandoc.cabal (and the other three cabal files) declare `license: GPL-2.0-or-later`; COPYRIGHT says "released under the [GPL], version 2 or later". The official 3.12 binaries were built from the immediately preceding commit 1539a541f5f7239c6f0a221985f24d1d7be6062a (changelog.md only difference).
